name: Notes in the diff's columns, and a new sidebar

pr.title: Line up a file's top notes with its diff, and show a lone pull request as a stack of one
pr.head: d573c3e874886dbb105a30fee597955bd27e8cbf

summary: A summary page is the guided review page that project summary publish puts on a repository's Projector site. Each file on the page is a card: a header, an optional one-line description, the notes about the file, and then its diff as one table per hunk. A note is a reviewer's remark, tagged context, verified, or concern. A note can sit under one line of the diff, at the top of a card about the whole file, or at the top of a section about several files. The sidebar on the left shows the pull request's stack, the projects it changes, the sections, and the published versions of the summary.

Notes under a line already render as rows of the diff table, with the tag in the line-number gutter and the text where the code starts. The other notes were bulleted lists, so their tags and text lined up with nothing in the diffs. This pull request makes the top notes on a card the same kind of row, in a small table that shares the diff's columns. A section's notes get the same layout as grid rows, with the tag in a column as wide as the diff's gutter. Every note on the page now starts its text at the same distance from the edge of its box.
It also reworks the sidebar and makes smaller changes:

• A stack of one. The sidebar lists every pull request in a stack, one row each, with the current one highlighted. A pull request with no stack showed only its title in grey. It now shows the same list with one highlighted row. The build's data does not change: only the page draws the row.
  • Projects as rows. The projects a pull request changes were a line of links reading "Projects: …" below the stack. They are now rows above the stack, styled like the stack's, with a folder icon where a stack row has its number.
  • Versions behind an icon. The list of published versions opens from a history icon instead of a "Versions · N" label. The icon's tooltip and accessible name read "Versions (N)". The current version is marked with the secondary surface colour.
  • Plainer links. The page header's Conversation, Files, and Compare links are spaced apart with a gap instead of dot separators, and are no longer underlined. The sidebar's Overview and Files links share one line.
  • More room in rows. Note rows get 13px of padding above and below their text instead of 5px, and the sidebar's stack rows get 8px instead of 3px.
  • Notes, not Review notes. A section's list of notes is headed Notes, and the page's "How to read this" paragraph says "Notes come in three kinds".

cards.title: Review status at this head
cards.html:
• The first Projector review asked for one change: a line in docs/cli.md that the edit left unwrapped. The author rewrapped it, and later reviews found it fixed.
  • The author took the first review's suggestion to drop notesList's unused class parameter.
  • The reviews at 965ed38, 4ae7cf2, and this head are clean. At this head the repository's gate passes: the site's type check and lint, the build (which reproduced the committed JavaScript exactly), all 505 unit tests, project check, and both plugin validations.
  • The pull request's description still describes an earlier head: it gives 9px for note padding, expects 503 tests, and does not mention the sidebar or header changes. The review suggests updating it before merging, since a squash merge makes it the commit message.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Card: one file's block on the summary page, rendered by renderFile.
  • Top notes: the notes on a whole file, with no line. The code calls them loose.
  • Note row: a tr.noterow, with the tag in the gutter cell td.ngut and the text in td.nte.
  • Stack: the chain of pull requests whose bases are each other's heads. The build stores it as data.stack, empty for a pull request that stands alone.
  • Section notes: the notes on a whole section, drawn by notesList in a box headed Notes.

groups.title: The page renderer
groups.kicker: Notes line up with the diff's columns, the sidebar gets project rows, a one-row stack, and a versions icon, and the header links lose their dots.
intro: The summary renderer, site/src/summary.ts, builds the whole page in the browser from the summary's data. renderFile draws one card per file. Before this change it drew a note under a line as a table row inside the diff, and drew the top notes through notesList, the same bulleted list a section uses for its own notes.

Now renderFile has one function, noteRow, that turns any note into a table row. The diff's rows call it for notes under a line, and the top notes go through it into a separate table placed above the diff. That table gets the same class and the same <colgroup> as the diff's hunk tables, so its gutter is exactly as wide as theirs.

A section's notes stay a list, but each item is now a three-column grid: the tag, right-aligned in a 92px column, then the text, then a concern's checkbox. The diff's gutter is also 92px wide, two 46px columns or one 92px column, so a section's note text starts where a file's note text does. The Notes heading is indented by the same 100px, the gutter plus the code cell's 8px padding.

In the sidebar, projectsList now draws the projects as a ul.stack.projects placed before the stack, headsList puts an icon in the versions toggle, and the header's links drop their dot separators for a flex gap. The stylesheet drops the rules for the old .prmeta line, the old .prtitle title, and the versions chevron.

checks.text: The compiled site/assets/summary.js is the TypeScript's build output and ships with the change. Rebuilding it at this head produced no difference.

files.note: Adds noteRow and the top-notes table in renderFile, reorders section notes, adds the folder and history icons, draws projects as sidebar rows, and makes stackList fall back to a one-row stack.

checks.text: A section's concern checkbox moves after the text. The checkbox handler still marks box.closest('li, tr'), so a checked concern dims its row. No CSS or script reads the removed <span class="nbox"> placeholder. I traced both.
A concern note's checkbox is keyed by the file's path, the same scope the top-notes list used at the base, so a concern a reader already checked stays checked. I traced it in the code.
The top table holds no tr.add, tr.del, or tr.ctx rows and no .src spans, so syntax highlighting and token marking, which read only those, leave it alone. I traced highlightFile and the token marker.
The table keeps the fnotes class, so the stylesheet's rules for collapsed and reviewed files still remove its border and hide it.
The label is built from a number only, so it needs no escaping in the attribute.

stackList uses data.stack only when it lists two or more pull requests. Otherwise it draws one current row from the pull request itself. The current row returns before it reads url, so the empty url is never used. A test checks the rendered row.
Each project URL and title goes through esc, as the old .prmeta links did.
The links now sit side by side with no text between them. The stylesheet's flex gap on .top .sub spaces them, so a page without the stylesheet shows them run together.

files.note: Styles section notes as gutter-aligned rows, lets the diff's note-row rules style the top notes, adds project rows and the versions icon button, spaces the header and sidebar links with gaps, widens row padding, and drops the unused .prtitle, .prmeta, and versions chevron rules.

checks.text: The new rules select .notes li. The file header's note badge is a span.badge.notes with no list items, so these rules leave it alone.
This padding applies to every note row in a diff, both under a line and at the top of a card.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Node-rendered tests cover the new markup, and the CLI reference names the stack of one.
intro: FileHeaderTests in tests/test_site.py builds a summary and renders it with the compiled script under node. One test now gives a file a note on the whole file and the section a note of its own, and checks the markup of both. New tests check that a pull request with an empty stack shows one highlighted row, that the projects render as rows before the stack, and that the versions toggle is an icon labelled with the count. They skip when node is missing.
docs/cli.md describes the site's sidebar, and gains a clause saying that a pull request with no stack is a stack of one, with its own row highlighted.

checks.text: The expected markup pins the exact column group: two lncol columns for a file with both sides.
